Question B-006-003-003.

Why the correct answer is right: Coax is popular because it is practical in many real installations: it can run near equipment and supports, pass through walls, tolerate weather when properly jacketed, and connect directly to common radios.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Less loss": Open-wire line often has lower loss than coax, so minimum loss alone does not explain why most stations still use coax.
- sourceIndex 2: "More power handling capability": Some coax handles high power and some does not; balanced open-wire line can also handle substantial power.
- sourceIndex 3: "Less expensive": Price varies by cable type and installation hardware, so cost is not the broad technical reason coax dominates amateur stations.
